description:
## Why

Foundation for all multiuser work. Every other sub-issue depends on a stable user identity model.

## What

Add a users table to the mail SQLite database:

```sql
CREATE TABLE users (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    username TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    display_name TEXT,
    email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    is_admin INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    quota_bytes INTEGER,  -- NULL = unlimited
    created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
```

Wire the existing CredentialStore (which already supports multiple users) to this table so that authenticated username → user row → user_id is a fast lookup at request time.

Provisioning CLI subcommand: `stoa-mail user add <username> <email> [--admin] [--quota-gb N]`, `stoa-mail user remove <username>`, `stoa-mail user list`, `stoa-mail user set-quota <username> <gb>`.

## Acceptance

- users table created via migration
- stoa-mail user add/remove/list/set-quota subcommands work
- Authenticated session resolves to a user_id within one SQL lookup
- Existing single-user deployments continue to work (migration seeds a default user from the existing auth.users config)
notes: The migration must seed the users table from the existing [[auth.users]] config so single-user deployments upgrade without manual intervention.
title: User accounts table and provisioning CLI
